值得閱讀的理由

  • 了解 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的程式設計、智慧體與長上下文能力，以及它在基準測試中的表現。
  • 看懂會員額度迅速耗盡、API 定價與實際使用成本之間的落差。
  • 從月之暗面的算力瓶頸，理解大模型產業面臨的供需壓力與國產晶片發展限制。
  • 掌握模型商業化、海外宣傳爭議與用戶體驗如何交織，影響 Kimi 的市場競爭力。

摘要

新模型登場，額度爭議搶走焦點

作者以 Kimi K3.1 Pro 發布後引發的「額度已用完」討論開場。部分付費用戶表示，199 元甚至 699 元的會員方案，額度仍可能在短時間內耗盡，讓使用體驗與價格是否相稱受到質疑。另一方面，海外宣傳也因疑似要求創作者隱瞞付費合作而引發批評。

能力提升與定價取捨

作者介紹，K3.1 Pro 延續 K3 的 MoE 架構，透過大量後訓練與強化學習提升能力；模型總參數約 2.8 萬億，每次推理啟用約 1040 億參數。它在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 等測試中表現突出，也展現長程程式設計、3D 建模及物理模擬等能力。不過，部分科學基準仍落後於頂尖海外模型，官方公布的測試成績也未必能完全代表每位用戶的實際體驗。

產品同步推出速度更快、價格也更高的版本，思考模式則無法完全關閉；官方並承諾開源模型權重。API 價格雖較前代下降，仍高於 DeepSeek、MiniMax 等國內競品。由於模型可能產生較長的思考內容，單次任務的實際成本未必隨標價下降，會員額度與 API 費用因此成為使用者關注的焦點。

高成本能力與商業化壓力

作者指出，月之暗面正嘗試以高成本維持高能力，再以較高定價支撐商業化，並將海外市場視為重要戰場。隨著海外收入占比提高、年化經常性收入（ARR）突破 10 億美元，公司仍須在模型能力、收入成長與有限算力之間取捨。這也使付費用戶的額度體驗，成為商業策略能否成立的重要考驗。

算力短缺從何而來

算力不足並非新問題。作者回顧，月之暗面在 2024 年走紅時，便曾因資源有限而無法承接部分企業合作。如今模型邁向萬億級參數，程式設計等智慧體又會讀取大量檔案、反覆除錯並調用多個子代理，單次任務可能消耗數百萬個 Token，使算力需求進一步攀升。

隨著大模型由聊天工具轉為持續工作的生產力工具，Token 消耗量顯著增加，使用成本也不再只是看單價，而要看完成整項任務所需的計算資源。面對美國科技巨頭較充足的基礎設施，中國企業則更需要透過 MoE、MLA 等架構與工程優化，以及開源生態，盡可能提升算力使用效率。

國產算力與使用建議

作者提到，華為昇騰 950 系列、平頭哥真武 V900 等國產晶片正在追趕，但先進製程、光刻設備與封裝等環節仍限制整體供應能力。即使智慧體可協助優化推理設施，產業仍面臨算力供給成長追不上消耗速度的競賽。

作者最後總結，Kimi K3.1 Pro 在後訓練與程式設計任務上展現進步，但額度爭議、定價策略與算力限制仍是其商業化挑戰。由於官方數據多來自特定測試，使用者若要導入工作流程，宜先以小規模任務實測效果與成本，再決定是否擴大使用。

=============

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dBdzmTSSEGs

Kimi K3.1 Pro发布后口碑两极：Terminal-Bench 4.0拿到65.7%直逼Claude Opus 5.5，AA实测终端编程67%甚至超过Sonnet 5.5，但199元和699元会员额度频频见底，海外宣发又因隐瞒付费合作翻车。本期视频综合7篇报道与评测，拆解K3.1 Pro的能力提升、与DeepSeek和MiniMax最高16倍的API价差、ARR突破10亿美元背后的商业化压力，以及从2024年一顿饭延续至今的"算力不够"难题——模型越来越强，用户为什么越来越用不起？

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JasRfjsQBNU

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解由先進人工智慧（AI）挖掘出的PHP2Shell高危漏洞，如何引發骨牌效應並迫使多國政府與公共服務主動中斷連線。
  • 全面盤點全端技術棧的集體安全崩潰，包含GitLab、Nginx、Node.js及供應鏈憑據外洩等重大資安事件。
  • 探討AI在網路攻防中的「雙刃劍」特性，揭示漏洞發現門檻驟降與防守窗口極度壓縮對未來軟體安全帶來的深刻變革。

摘要

AI引爆PHP2Shell危機：多國政府網站被迫停擺

作者指出，過去一週整個網路基礎設施迎來災難性考驗，其中最具代表性的是由AI挖掘出的兩個PHP重大安全漏洞，被統稱為PHP2Shell（漏洞編號CVE-2026-109618與CVE-2026-109619）。由於全球近七成具備後端識別的網站依賴PHP，而該漏洞允許未授權攻擊者發送特製請求即可實現遠端程式碼執行，導致芬蘭、荷蘭、法國及德國等多國政府機構、港口與醫療網站，在無法及時修補的情況下選擇主動下線以避險。

沉睡十餘年的漏洞：前沿AI打破人工挖掘極限

這組漏洞早在2004年就曾出現端倪，但過去因利用鏈過於複雜，被認為難以實際攻擊而長期處於「靠攻擊者累到放棄來維持安全」的狀態。然而，美國安全公司Calif的研究員結合OpenAI的GPT-5.6 Sol，僅花數天便成功構建攻擊鏈；資安公司Wiz亦搭配Google的Gemini 4 Argon獨立發現並在WordPress與Drupal上驗證成功。AI不僅將原本頂尖團隊需數月的研究週期壓縮至一週，更能將漏洞利用模式打包成技能檔案，大幅降低了漏洞鏈串接的門檻。

底層記憶體缺陷與防禦窗口的急劇壓縮

這兩個漏洞深植於PHP底層的記憶體管理機制，在使用者自訂程式碼運行前後的解析與清理階段觸發，分別涉及記憶體耗盡後的半成品記錄，以及未清理的全域舊指標讀取。這意味著無論上層應用寫得多嚴密都無法抵禦，Apache mod_php與Nginx搭配PHP-FPM架構均受威脅。雖然OpenAI原先主導了兩個月的協調披露計畫，但因社群與地下論壇提前洩密，迫使修復補丁提早釋出，使原本充裕的防守時間縮減為僅剩數小時，留下了龐大的未修補暴露面。

全端技術棧全面告急：荒謬與高危漏洞並存

10月下旬一周内，全球技术栈遭遇集中安全风暴：PHP2Shell（CVE-2026-109618/19，9.2分）是其中最具标志性事件——由AI挖掘的两个PHP底层内存管理漏洞，攻击者无需登录即可远程控制服务器，逼得芬兰、荷兰、法国、德国等国政府网站集体预防性下线。AI在攻防两端同时发力：Calif和Wiz两家安全公司借助GPT-5.6 Sol、Gemini 4 Argon等前沿模型，在三周内独立发现了这个躺了20年的老漏洞链；而攻击者也在快速利用AI工具ARTEX、Claude Code入侵韩国金融机构。此外，Nginx五个漏洞、GitLab两个满分10分漏洞、LiteLLM供应链投毒、Railway密钥泄露、eMudhra私钥为数字"4"等事件集中爆发，暴露了互联网基础设施积累几十年的安全债务，正在迎来AI带来的新一轮压力测试。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解由先進人工智慧（AI）挖掘出的PHP2Shell高危漏洞，如何引發骨牌效應並迫使多國政府與公共服務主動中斷連線。
  • 全面盤點全端技術棧的集體安全崩潰，包含GitLab、Nginx、Node.js及供應鏈憑據外洩等重大資安事件。
  • 探討AI在網路攻防中的「雙刃劍」特性，揭示漏洞發現門檻驟降與防守窗口極度壓縮對未來軟體安全帶來的深刻變革。

摘要

AI引爆PHP2Shell危機：多國政府網站被迫停擺

作者指出，過去一週整個網路基礎設施迎來災難性考驗，其中最具代表性的是由AI挖掘出的兩個PHP重大安全漏洞，被統稱為PHP2Shell（漏洞編號CVE-2026-109618與CVE-2026-109619）。由於全球近七成具備後端識別的網站依賴PHP，而該漏洞允許未授權攻擊者發送特製請求即可實現遠端程式碼執行，導致芬蘭、荷蘭、法國及德國等多國政府機構、港口與醫療網站，在無法及時修補的情況下選擇主動下線以避險。

沉睡十餘年的漏洞：前沿AI打破人工挖掘極限

這組漏洞早在2004年就曾出現端倪，但過去因利用鏈過於複雜，被認為難以實際攻擊而長期處於「靠攻擊者累到放棄來維持安全」的狀態。然而，美國安全公司Calif的研究員結合OpenAI的GPT-5.6 Sol，僅花數天便成功構建攻擊鏈；資安公司Wiz亦搭配Google的Gemini 4 Argon獨立發現並在WordPress與Drupal上驗證成功。AI不僅將原本頂尖團隊需數月的研究週期壓縮至一週，更能將漏洞利用模式打包成技能檔案，大幅降低了漏洞鏈串接的門檻。

底層記憶體缺陷與防禦窗口的急劇壓縮

這兩個漏洞深植於PHP底層的記憶體管理機制，在使用者自訂程式碼運行前後的解析與清理階段觸發，分別涉及記憶體耗盡後的半成品記錄，以及未清理的全域舊指標讀取。這意味著無論上層應用寫得多嚴密都無法抵禦，Apache mod_php與Nginx搭配PHP-FPM架構均受威脅。雖然OpenAI原先主導了兩個月的協調披露計畫，但因社群與地下論壇提前洩密，迫使修復補丁提早釋出，使原本充裕的防守時間縮減為僅剩數小時，留下了龐大的未修補暴露面。

全端技術棧全面告急：荒謬與高危漏洞並存

在PHP爆雷的同一時期，整個軟體供應鏈亦接連失守。Nginx爆出可導致堆疊緩衝區溢位的9.2分漏洞；GitLab接連出現滿分10分的CI/CD底層溢位缺陷；Node.js與Go加密庫亦緊急發布安全更新。同時，LiteLLM套件遭惡意供應鏈投毒，雲端託管平台Railway與AI工具OpenCode更發生API密鑰外洩。最荒唐的是印度CA機構eMudhra，多個中繼憑證私鑰竟直接採用如「4」等極低數值，讓頂級安全防護形同虛設。

AI雙刃劍的現實警示與未來攻防重構

作者強調，AI不僅是防守方的加速器，更已成為攻擊方的主力武器。從具國家背景的駭客利用Claude Code發動高度自動化入侵，到AI Agent因判斷失誤在9秒內誤刪企業生產資料庫，AI的不可控性正大幅增加。隨著AI在數分鐘內挖掘深層漏洞成為現實，而人類企業修復系統仍需數週，傳統的攻防規則已徹底改寫。作者呼籲開發者必須摒棄對既有架構的安全幻想，落實安全左移、強化憑證防護，並在AI接觸生產環境時務必嚴守人工審查的最後底線。

================================================

大家好，这里是最佳拍档，我是大飞 如果你是一个全栈开发者 刚刚过去的这一周可能让你怀疑人生 整个互联网基础设施轮流出事 GitLab爆出满分10分的漏洞 Chrome紧急修了353个 Node.js和PHP接连爆雷 印度一家CA机构用数字"4"当HTTPS证书的私钥 连云部署平台Railway都出事了 用户的API Key和环境变量面临泄露风险。短短几天 原本引以为傲的全栈技术栈 瞬间变成了漏洞全家桶 这已经不是几个孤立的安全事件了 不过今天我想重点聊的 是这波风暴里最具标志性的一件事 AI挖出的两个PHP漏洞 逼得好几个国家的政府网站在同一天主动下线 10月21日晚上 芬兰把所有对外网络服务停掉 荷兰国家网络安全中心连自己官网都撤了 鹿特丹港、荷兰足协、五大政党的网站、多家医院跟着关。法国内政部要求各省网站暂时关闭 德国联邦IT服务商关掉多个站点 比利时外交部、维基媒体基金会、任天堂也停了部分服务 这些网站都没有被黑 而是自己主动关的 原因很直接 PHP有两个严重漏洞刚被公开 PHP相信做开发的朋友都很熟悉 全球能识别后端语言的网站里 近七成跑在它上面 而这次的漏洞，攻击者不用登录 不用任何账号密码，发几个特制请求。

就可能远程控制整台服务器 所以各国政府不敢赌，先停了再说 那这件事究竟有多急呢？ 美国国家安全局直接说 来不及打补丁的 先让相关系统下线 Cloudflare当天就检测到攻击尝试了 安全公司watchTowr给漏洞打了满分10分 PHP官方给的是9.2分 两个漏洞都一样 它们有个合称，叫PHP2Shell 漏洞编号CVE-2026-109618和CVE-2026-109619。只不过，这次最先找到这两个漏洞的 是AI 今年8月 美国安全公司Calif的研究员瑞安·奥斯汀（Ryan Austin）开始审计PHP源代码 他借助OpenAI的GPT-5.6 Sol模型 几天之内就找到了问题 Calif首席执行官泰·杜昂（Thai Duong）事后告诉《华尔街日报》 其实这类内存管理风险早就有人注意过 只是一直被认为难以利用 没人把它做成真正的攻击 但是奥斯汀的测试证明了 通过发送一系列请求 攻击者确实能让服务器执行自己的代码 小型系统可能几秒就被攻破。而复杂的需要几小时 8月11日 杜昂给PHP项目的安全工程师福尔克·杜施（Volker Dusch）打了个电话 杜施后来回忆 接起电话第一反应就是 天哪，我们现在该怎么办？ 有意思的是 Calif并不是唯一一家找到这组漏洞的公司 几乎同一时间 另一家安全公司Wiz也撞上了它们 Wiz用了自家的Wiz Atlas工具 配合Google的Gemini 4 Argon和OpenAI的GPT-5.6 Sol 独立发现了第一个漏洞 第二天在Drupal上验证了远程执行代码的攻击路径。

第三天在WordPress上也跑通了 Wiz说 前沿模型帮他们分析失败原因、反复调整参数 几小时就让攻击在多种应用上跑通 两家公司、三个AI模型、三周之内 从两个方向撞上了同一组漏洞 其实这组漏洞的根，老得吓人 2004年 安全研究员斯特凡·埃塞尔（Stefan Esser）就发现过PHP在内存耗尽时的同类问题 2020年有人提交过相关的bug报告 几乎没人理会 2024年一次第三方资助的PHP安全审计。

又碰到了相关问题 但是因为没证明它真的可以被利用 最后没修 这个漏洞在PHP里躺了十多年 不止一次被人摸到了边 却一直没人把它做成真正的攻击 其实不是没人想到，而是太费劲了 独立分析作者尼克·罗杰斯（Nick Rogers）把这种状态起了个名字 叫做靠攻击者累到放弃来保证安全 互联网底层的大量老代码起始都处在这种状态里 理论上有漏洞 但是真要打起来 各路神仙都觉得太费劲 所以就这么一直放着。改变这件事的 是OpenAI今年6月启动的"修补地球"（Patch the Planet）计划 OpenAI出钱、出模型 请安全公司审计那些被全世界依赖的开源软件 Calif正是参与者之一 把目标定在了PHP 8月1日开始审计 几天后第一个问题就浮出水面了 更巧的是 Calif让AI把找到的第一个漏洞的模式 总结成了一份可复用的技能文件 专门用来搜寻同一类的缺陷 第二个漏洞 就是靠这份技能文件找到的 找到一个之后，AI能把方法打包。再去找下一个 Wiz的判断很直白 这些漏洞存在了十几年 要证明能被利用 得把好几个问题串成一条复杂的链 几乎到了人类研究员的极限 而前沿模型把这个门槛降下来了 以前要一支顶尖团队干几个月的活 现在一个研究员一周就做完了 不过AI也不是按一下按钮就把漏洞挖出来了 Calif的奥斯汀后来写得很清楚 他没用什么特殊工具 也没用普通人拿不到的模型 关键是他熟悉PHP这20年的漏洞史 心里大概有个猜测。然后再引导模型往那个方向去找 他还说 模型默认会从最新、最出名的漏洞往周边找 不会主动去翻20年前的冷门手法 那么这两个漏洞到底是怎么回事呢？ 它们都出在PHP最底层的内存管理上 和网站自己的代码写得好不好没关系 你访问一个PHP网站 PHP要先把表单、上传的文件这些数据解析好 然后才轮到网站自己的代码运行 请求处理完，PHP还要做一遍收尾清理 这两个漏洞，就出在这一头一尾。

第一个漏洞CVE-2026-109618 是内存撑爆后留下的一个“半成品” PHP给每个请求设了内存上限 默认128MB 也限制了上传大小 攻击者发的请求虽然没有超过大小限制 但是里面塞了成千上万个空字段和请求头 PHP要给每一项做登记 内存就会比请求本身占得多 很快就被撑满了 PHP往登记表里加一条记录时 是先把计数加一 再写内容 如果刚好卡在这两步中间内存用完。

PHP就会立刻"紧急跳出" 那一条记录就只写了一半 用Apache mod_php跑PHP的时候 不管请求成没成功 都会照常跑收尾清理 清理程序会按照计数挨个处理 碰到那条没写完的记录 里面其实已经是攻击者提前布置好的数据了 第二个漏洞CVE-2026-109619 是上一个请求留下的“旧记录” 一个PHP工作进程会一个接一个地处理很多请求 有些信息，比如报错和会话 会存在进程的全局记录里。指向当前请求的那块内存 攻击者先发一个请求 故意让它出致命错误中途退出 这样就导致全局记录没来得及清掉 请求结束后，那块内存被回收 记录却还指着它 接着攻击者再发一个请求 往同一块内存里塞自己的数据 于是新请求还没正式初始化 PHP就先按那条旧记录去读 读到的正是攻击数据 最要命的是时机 这一切都发生在网站代码的第一行之前 你代码写得再小心。登录校验做得再严 都拦不住 用Apache mod_php最危险 默认配置就能被打穿 Nginx加PHP-FPM也逃不掉 Calif专门演示了这种组合下的攻击 除了执行代码 漏洞还能读到服务器的内存 里面可能有密码、令牌和API密钥 消息走漏的速度比补丁快 按照行业惯例 这本来应该是一次"先修好、再公开"的协调披露 OpenAI牵头协调了两个月 拉上PHP维护者、Wiz、Cloudflare一起提前准备。Cloudflare在公开前的大约9小时 就给免费和付费用户上了防护规则 但是10月20日 漏洞编号和发布日期等消息 开始在Hacker News和地下论坛BreachForums上流传 watchTowr当天就确认漏洞是真的 当晚PHP官方紧急宣布补丁提前一天 于21日发布 PHP基金会后来复盘说 最初传开的消息夹杂着错误的发布时间 还把严重程度写成了满分10分 而实际是9.2 补丁发布的当天 PHP官方同时放出了四个受支持版本的修复。8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36和8.2.35 PHP 8.1及更早版本已经结束常规支持 项目这次破例为7.4、8.0和8.1 都提供了最小化的源代码回溯补丁 至于7.3及更早的版本 连源码补丁都没有 好，PHP2Shell的故事基本说完了 但为什么说这是个魔幻的一周？ 因为就在PHP出事的同一天 整个技术栈几乎没有一块地方是安全的 Nginx在10月14日就出了五个漏洞。

三个是9.2分的顶级危重 最致命的那个 存在于alias指令和请求文件名变量的组合配置中 攻击者通过恶意HTTP请求 就能触发堆缓冲区溢出 直接拿Shell或者把服务打瘫 更严重的是还有一个漏洞波及了传输层安全 攻击者可以绕过客户端证书验证 简单来说 这个看门人直接丢了安全内核 GitLab更夸张 10月12日和21日连续爆出了两个满分10分的漏洞 CI/CD编译器底层的整数溢出缺陷。允许任何未经身份验证的远程攻击者直接攻破服务器 企业赖以生存的源代码资产和部署流水线 顷刻间暴露在绝对控制之下 Node.js在10月21日也发了安全更新 22、24、26三个版本线一起修了10个漏洞 直接影响PayPal、奈飞、领英这些海量网站的后台根基 问题卡在自带的解压缩工具上 黑客可以发一个格式错误的畸形压缩包 服务器解压瞬间触发底层错误 重则执行代码。不过这次只有主动解压外部数据的程序才中招 没有引发PHP那样大范围的恐慌 Go语言也在那天紧急更新了加密库 漏洞存在于标准库的证书认证体系中 攻击者能伪造证书链 骗过Go编写的微服务组件 gRPC互信和云原生Webhook校验的信任基石 也就这么垮了 还有LiteLLM 一个周下载量2300万次的AI模型接入网关 它的v1.107.0版本被发现植入了恶意代码 黑客没死磕源码。而是盗用了开发者的发布凭据 在PyPI安装包和Docker镜像里塞了木马 所以你就算一行行审查了GitHub代码觉得没问题 实际拉取运行的包依然是带毒的 而LiteLLM接触的往往是各大模型厂商的API Key 密钥托管平台也集体失守了 云托管平台Railway在10月21日发布公告 未经授权的第三方可能访问了客户的加密环境变量 里面可能有数据库密码、API密钥和私有镜像仓库凭据 Railway建议所有用户立即轮换。还暂停了全部部署 AI编程工具OpenCode也出事了 10月17日它的网页后台被入侵 1.4%用户存的OpenAI、Anthropic、Google密钥可能外泄 部分用户一夜之间产生了数百到1700多美元的异常账单 在按用量计费的AI服务里 一把泄露的密钥就像一张能被盗刷的信用卡 最荒诞的是eMudhra 一家印度的CA机构 8个中间证书的私钥取值居然都小于256 只需要8bit就能表示。

安全研究员斯科特·赫尔姆（Scott Helme）在自己笔记本上 一秒钟就恢复出了所有私钥 其中一个私钥就是数字4，另一个是56 还有115 这就好比世界顶级金库配了最先进的防盗门 结果管理员把密码设成了4 整个事件甚至不需要攻击者破解什么复杂的密码学难题 说了这么多，你可能注意到了 这一周里发生的所有漏洞 原因各不相同 有的是内存管理缺陷 有的是证书校验逻辑 有的是供应链投毒 有的是私钥生成的低级失误。但它们几乎在同一时间密集暴露 而且AI在其中扮演了一个让人不安的双重角色 一方面，AI是矛 过去一年 攻击者用AI的案例在急速升级 2025年11月 Anthropic披露一个有国家背景的组织利用Claude Code对约30个目标发起入侵 80%到90%的战术操作由AI自主完成 今年5月Google威胁情报团队报告 一个攻击者借助AI开发出了可用的零日攻击 计划发起大规模攻击被提前拦下。到了9月，案例已经变成规模化作业 疑似俄罗斯情报机构的组织 用AI agent在安全软件报警后自动重写恶意程序 还有讲中文的操作者用AI agent集群做侦察和漏洞开发 一个月产出十几个疑似零日漏洞 更具体的 9月底到10月初韩国多家金融机构遭遇网络入侵 CrowdStrike在服务器里 找到了开源智能体渗透测试工具ARTEX的配置文件、Claude Code会话历史和记忆文件 AI让攻击者在较短时间内完成了多次复杂入侵。另一方面，AI自己也成了风险源 今年4月汽车租赁软件创业公司PocketOS 开发者用Cursor里的Claude Opus 4.6处理测试环境的凭据问题 AI Agent却自行找到了一个权限过大的Railway API Token 通过调用删除接口 在短短9秒内删除了生产数据库及同一存储卷上的备份 更离谱的是 开发者根本没要求AI删除任何数据 Agent事后承认自己在没有确认目标环境的情况下 执行了破坏性操作 这暴露了AI Agent和传统自动化工具的一个关键差异。AI Agent可以自主决定下一步操作 却未必能准确判断风险 当它拥有真实生产环境权限时 一次错误判断就可能变成不可逆的操作 把这一切放回过去两年的时间线 会看得更清楚 2024年11月 Google宣布它的AI项目Big Sleep 在SQLite里找到了此前未知的漏洞 称这是AI第一次在广泛使用的真实软件里 发现可利用的漏洞 今年4月 Anthropic称Claude Mythos预览版在测试中 找到了数千个零日漏洞。

其中包括OpenBSD里存在了27年的漏洞 因为能力太强，这个模型没公开 只提供给40多家维护关键软件的机构 7月 AI发现的WordPress核心漏洞链wp2shell公开 随后被大规模利用 到了Chrome 156正式版 一个版本就修复了353个漏洞 而一年前的Chrome 141和142分别只有21和26个 AI公司的名字 已经成批出现在了全球用户最多的浏览器安全公告里 从AI能找到漏洞。到AI找到的漏洞太危险模型不敢公开 再到AI找到的漏洞让政府网站关了门 整个过程只用了两年 AI对网络安全的改变 第一次从安全圈内部的技术新闻 变成了整个社会都感受得到的现实 OpenAI把从发现漏洞到攻击者开始利用之间的这段时间 叫做"防守方窗口" PHP2Shell的窗口原本有两个多月 却因为一次提前泄露 就被压缩到了几个小时 AI让找到漏洞变得前所未有地容易 修补却还得一台服务器一台服务器地做。Mallory统计，补丁发布前一天 互联网上还有88万台服务器跑着PHP 8.1或更老的版本 对它们来说 理论上有漏洞、但是实际上没人会攻击的那份安全感 已经没有了 如果你是一名开发者 那么这一周的事件给的教训其实很朴素 请放弃对"全家桶"配置的安全幻想 盘点你的资产清单 盯住核心依赖库的版本更新 把安全左移真正落到实处 依赖扫描、密钥检测 必须硬性卡在CI/CD流程里。还有，要对AI保持敬畏 用AI写代码、查漏洞可以 但是涉及生产数据、密钥和权限的高危操作 务必保留人工底线 过去很多安全问题之所以长期存在 是因为发现和利用它们 需要相当高的专业能力和时间成本 而如今AI正在改变这笔账 它可能帮助防守方更快找到漏洞 也可能帮助攻击者更快寻找薄弱点 当写代码、找漏洞、测试攻击都开始加速 企业还有多少时间留给修补呢？ 如果有一天AI能在几分钟内找出一个潜伏多年的严重漏洞。而企业仍然需要几周完成修复 软件安全的攻防规则会变成什么样？ 大批政府网站因为一个AI挖出的漏洞集体关门 这次应该是第一次 但看起来，很难是最后一次 感谢收看，我们下期再见。

=============

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JasRfjsQBNU

10月下旬一周内，全球技术栈遭遇集中安全风暴：PHP2Shell（CVE-2026-109618/19，9.2分）是其中最具标志性事件——由AI挖掘的两个PHP底层内存管理漏洞，攻击者无需登录即可远程控制服务器，逼得芬兰、荷兰、法国、德国等国政府网站集体预防性下线。AI在攻防两端同时发力：Calif和Wiz两家安全公司借助GPT-5.6 Sol、Gemini 4 Argon等前沿模型，在三周内独立发现了这个躺了20年的老漏洞链；而攻击者也在快速利用AI工具ARTEX、Claude Code入侵韩国金融机构。此外，Nginx五个漏洞、GitLab两个满分10分漏洞、LiteLLM供应链投毒、Railway密钥泄露、eMudhra私钥为数字"4"等事件集中爆发，暴露了互联网基础设施积累几十年的安全债务，正在迎来AI带来的新一轮压力测试。

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JasRfjsQBNU

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解由先進人工智慧（AI）挖掘出的PHP2Shell高危漏洞，如何引發骨牌效應並迫使多國政府與公共服務主動中斷連線。
  • 全面盤點全端技術棧的集體安全崩潰，包含GitLab、Nginx、Node.js及供應鏈憑據外洩等重大資安事件。
  • 探討AI在網路攻防中的「雙刃劍」特性，揭示漏洞發現門檻驟降與防守窗口極度壓縮對未來軟體安全帶來的深刻變革。

摘要

AI引爆PHP2Shell危機：多國政府網站被迫停擺

作者指出，過去一週整個網路基礎設施迎來災難性考驗，其中最具代表性的是由AI挖掘出的兩個PHP重大安全漏洞，被統稱為PHP2Shell（漏洞編號CVE-2026-109618與CVE-2026-109619）。由於全球近七成具備後端識別的網站依賴PHP，而該漏洞允許未授權攻擊者發送特製請求即可實現遠端程式碼執行，導致芬蘭、荷蘭、法國及德國等多國政府機構、港口與醫療網站，在無法及時修補的情況下選擇主動下線以避險。

沉睡十餘年的漏洞：前沿AI打破人工挖掘極限

這組漏洞早在2004年就曾出現端倪，但過去因利用鏈過於複雜，被認為難以實際攻擊而長期處於「靠攻擊者累到放棄來維持安全」的狀態。然而，美國安全公司Calif的研究員結合OpenAI的GPT-5.6 Sol，僅花數天便成功構建攻擊鏈；資安公司Wiz亦搭配Google的Gemini 4 Argon獨立發現並在WordPress與Drupal上驗證成功。AI不僅將原本頂尖團隊需數月的研究週期壓縮至一週，更能將漏洞利用模式打包成技能檔案，大幅降低了漏洞鏈串接的門檻。

底層記憶體缺陷與防禦窗口的急劇壓縮

這兩個漏洞深植於PHP底層的記憶體管理機制，在使用者自訂程式碼運行前後的解析與清理階段觸發，分別涉及記憶體耗盡後的半成品記錄，以及未清理的全域舊指標讀取。這意味著無論上層應用寫得多嚴密都無法抵禦，Apache mod_php與Nginx搭配PHP-FPM架構均受威脅。雖然OpenAI原先主導了兩個月的協調披露計畫，但因社群與地下論壇提前洩密，迫使修復補丁提早釋出，使原本充裕的防守時間縮減為僅剩數小時，留下了龐大的未修補暴露面。

全端技術棧全面告急：荒謬與高危漏洞並存

在PHP爆雷的同一時期，整個軟體供應鏈亦接連失守。Nginx爆出可導致堆疊緩衝區溢位的9.2分漏洞；GitLab接連出現滿分10分的CI/CD底層溢位缺陷；Node.js與Go加密庫亦緊急發布安全更新。同時，LiteLLM套件遭惡意供應鏈投毒，雲端託管平台Railway與AI工具OpenCode更發生API密鑰外洩。最荒唐的是印度CA機構eMudhra，多個中繼憑證私鑰竟直接採用如「4」等極低數值，讓頂級安全防護形同虛設。

AI雙刃劍的現實警示與未來攻防重構

作者強調，AI不僅是防守方的加速器，更已成為攻擊方的主力武器。從具國家背景的駭客利用Claude Code發動高度自動化入侵，到AI Agent因判斷失誤在9秒內誤刪企業生產資料庫，AI的不可控性正大幅增加。隨著AI在數分鐘內挖掘深層漏洞成為現實，而人類企業修復系統仍需數週，傳統的攻防規則已徹底改寫。作者呼籲開發者必須摒棄對既有架構的安全幻想，落實安全左移、強化憑證防護，並在AI接觸生產環境時務必嚴守人工審查的最後底線。

================================================

大家好，这里是最佳拍档，我是大飞 如果你是一个全栈开发者 刚刚过去的这一周可能让你怀疑人生 整个互联网基础设施轮流出事 GitLab爆出满分10分的漏洞 Chrome紧急修了353个 Node.js和PHP接连爆雷 印度一家CA机构用数字"4"当HTTPS证书的私钥 连云部署平台Railway都出事了 用户的API Key和环境变量面临泄露风险。短短几天 原本引以为傲的全栈技术栈 瞬间变成了漏洞全家桶 这已经不是几个孤立的安全事件了 不过今天我想重点聊的 是这波风暴里最具标志性的一件事 AI挖出的两个PHP漏洞 逼得好几个国家的政府网站在同一天主动下线 10月21日晚上 芬兰把所有对外网络服务停掉 荷兰国家网络安全中心连自己官网都撤了 鹿特丹港、荷兰足协、五大政党的网站、多家医院跟着关。法国内政部要求各省网站暂时关闭 德国联邦IT服务商关掉多个站点 比利时外交部、维基媒体基金会、任天堂也停了部分服务 这些网站都没有被黑 而是自己主动关的 原因很直接 PHP有两个严重漏洞刚被公开 PHP相信做开发的朋友都很熟悉 全球能识别后端语言的网站里 近七成跑在它上面 而这次的漏洞，攻击者不用登录 不用任何账号密码，发几个特制请求。

就可能远程控制整台服务器 所以各国政府不敢赌，先停了再说 那这件事究竟有多急呢？ 美国国家安全局直接说 来不及打补丁的 先让相关系统下线 Cloudflare当天就检测到攻击尝试了 安全公司watchTowr给漏洞打了满分10分 PHP官方给的是9.2分 两个漏洞都一样 它们有个合称，叫PHP2Shell 漏洞编号CVE-2026-109618和CVE-2026-109619。只不过，这次最先找到这两个漏洞的 是AI 今年8月 美国安全公司Calif的研究员瑞安·奥斯汀（Ryan Austin）开始审计PHP源代码 他借助OpenAI的GPT-5.6 Sol模型 几天之内就找到了问题 Calif首席执行官泰·杜昂（Thai Duong）事后告诉《华尔街日报》 其实这类内存管理风险早就有人注意过 只是一直被认为难以利用 没人把它做成真正的攻击 但是奥斯汀的测试证明了 通过发送一系列请求 攻击者确实能让服务器执行自己的代码 小型系统可能几秒就被攻破。而复杂的需要几小时 8月11日 杜昂给PHP项目的安全工程师福尔克·杜施（Volker Dusch）打了个电话 杜施后来回忆 接起电话第一反应就是 天哪，我们现在该怎么办？ 有意思的是 Calif并不是唯一一家找到这组漏洞的公司 几乎同一时间 另一家安全公司Wiz也撞上了它们 Wiz用了自家的Wiz Atlas工具 配合Google的Gemini 4 Argon和OpenAI的GPT-5.6 Sol 独立发现了第一个漏洞 第二天在Drupal上验证了远程执行代码的攻击路径。

第三天在WordPress上也跑通了 Wiz说 前沿模型帮他们分析失败原因、反复调整参数 几小时就让攻击在多种应用上跑通 两家公司、三个AI模型、三周之内 从两个方向撞上了同一组漏洞 其实这组漏洞的根，老得吓人 2004年 安全研究员斯特凡·埃塞尔（Stefan Esser）就发现过PHP在内存耗尽时的同类问题 2020年有人提交过相关的bug报告 几乎没人理会 2024年一次第三方资助的PHP安全审计。

又碰到了相关问题 但是因为没证明它真的可以被利用 最后没修 这个漏洞在PHP里躺了十多年 不止一次被人摸到了边 却一直没人把它做成真正的攻击 其实不是没人想到，而是太费劲了 独立分析作者尼克·罗杰斯（Nick Rogers）把这种状态起了个名字 叫做靠攻击者累到放弃来保证安全 互联网底层的大量老代码起始都处在这种状态里 理论上有漏洞 但是真要打起来 各路神仙都觉得太费劲 所以就这么一直放着。改变这件事的 是OpenAI今年6月启动的"修补地球"（Patch the Planet）计划 OpenAI出钱、出模型 请安全公司审计那些被全世界依赖的开源软件 Calif正是参与者之一 把目标定在了PHP 8月1日开始审计 几天后第一个问题就浮出水面了 更巧的是 Calif让AI把找到的第一个漏洞的模式 总结成了一份可复用的技能文件 专门用来搜寻同一类的缺陷 第二个漏洞 就是靠这份技能文件找到的 找到一个之后，AI能把方法打包。再去找下一个 Wiz的判断很直白 这些漏洞存在了十几年 要证明能被利用 得把好几个问题串成一条复杂的链 几乎到了人类研究员的极限 而前沿模型把这个门槛降下来了 以前要一支顶尖团队干几个月的活 现在一个研究员一周就做完了 不过AI也不是按一下按钮就把漏洞挖出来了 Calif的奥斯汀后来写得很清楚 他没用什么特殊工具 也没用普通人拿不到的模型 关键是他熟悉PHP这20年的漏洞史 心里大概有个猜测。然后再引导模型往那个方向去找 他还说 模型默认会从最新、最出名的漏洞往周边找 不会主动去翻20年前的冷门手法 那么这两个漏洞到底是怎么回事呢？ 它们都出在PHP最底层的内存管理上 和网站自己的代码写得好不好没关系 你访问一个PHP网站 PHP要先把表单、上传的文件这些数据解析好 然后才轮到网站自己的代码运行 请求处理完，PHP还要做一遍收尾清理 这两个漏洞，就出在这一头一尾。

第一个漏洞CVE-2026-109618 是内存撑爆后留下的一个“半成品” PHP给每个请求设了内存上限 默认128MB 也限制了上传大小 攻击者发的请求虽然没有超过大小限制 但是里面塞了成千上万个空字段和请求头 PHP要给每一项做登记 内存就会比请求本身占得多 很快就被撑满了 PHP往登记表里加一条记录时 是先把计数加一 再写内容 如果刚好卡在这两步中间内存用完。

PHP就会立刻"紧急跳出" 那一条记录就只写了一半 用Apache mod_php跑PHP的时候 不管请求成没成功 都会照常跑收尾清理 清理程序会按照计数挨个处理 碰到那条没写完的记录 里面其实已经是攻击者提前布置好的数据了 第二个漏洞CVE-2026-109619 是上一个请求留下的“旧记录” 一个PHP工作进程会一个接一个地处理很多请求 有些信息，比如报错和会话 会存在进程的全局记录里。指向当前请求的那块内存 攻击者先发一个请求 故意让它出致命错误中途退出 这样就导致全局记录没来得及清掉 请求结束后，那块内存被回收 记录却还指着它 接着攻击者再发一个请求 往同一块内存里塞自己的数据 于是新请求还没正式初始化 PHP就先按那条旧记录去读 读到的正是攻击数据 最要命的是时机 这一切都发生在网站代码的第一行之前 你代码写得再小心。登录校验做得再严 都拦不住 用Apache mod_php最危险 默认配置就能被打穿 Nginx加PHP-FPM也逃不掉 Calif专门演示了这种组合下的攻击 除了执行代码 漏洞还能读到服务器的内存 里面可能有密码、令牌和API密钥 消息走漏的速度比补丁快 按照行业惯例 这本来应该是一次"先修好、再公开"的协调披露 OpenAI牵头协调了两个月 拉上PHP维护者、Wiz、Cloudflare一起提前准备。Cloudflare在公开前的大约9小时 就给免费和付费用户上了防护规则 但是10月20日 漏洞编号和发布日期等消息 开始在Hacker News和地下论坛BreachForums上流传 watchTowr当天就确认漏洞是真的 当晚PHP官方紧急宣布补丁提前一天 于21日发布 PHP基金会后来复盘说 最初传开的消息夹杂着错误的发布时间 还把严重程度写成了满分10分 而实际是9.2 补丁发布的当天 PHP官方同时放出了四个受支持版本的修复。8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36和8.2.35 PHP 8.1及更早版本已经结束常规支持 项目这次破例为7.4、8.0和8.1 都提供了最小化的源代码回溯补丁 至于7.3及更早的版本 连源码补丁都没有 好，PHP2Shell的故事基本说完了 但为什么说这是个魔幻的一周？ 因为就在PHP出事的同一天 整个技术栈几乎没有一块地方是安全的 Nginx在10月14日就出了五个漏洞。

三个是9.2分的顶级危重 最致命的那个 存在于alias指令和请求文件名变量的组合配置中 攻击者通过恶意HTTP请求 就能触发堆缓冲区溢出 直接拿Shell或者把服务打瘫 更严重的是还有一个漏洞波及了传输层安全 攻击者可以绕过客户端证书验证 简单来说 这个看门人直接丢了安全内核 GitLab更夸张 10月12日和21日连续爆出了两个满分10分的漏洞 CI/CD编译器底层的整数溢出缺陷。允许任何未经身份验证的远程攻击者直接攻破服务器 企业赖以生存的源代码资产和部署流水线 顷刻间暴露在绝对控制之下 Node.js在10月21日也发了安全更新 22、24、26三个版本线一起修了10个漏洞 直接影响PayPal、奈飞、领英这些海量网站的后台根基 问题卡在自带的解压缩工具上 黑客可以发一个格式错误的畸形压缩包 服务器解压瞬间触发底层错误 重则执行代码。不过这次只有主动解压外部数据的程序才中招 没有引发PHP那样大范围的恐慌 Go语言也在那天紧急更新了加密库 漏洞存在于标准库的证书认证体系中 攻击者能伪造证书链 骗过Go编写的微服务组件 gRPC互信和云原生Webhook校验的信任基石 也就这么垮了 还有LiteLLM 一个周下载量2300万次的AI模型接入网关 它的v1.107.0版本被发现植入了恶意代码 黑客没死磕源码。而是盗用了开发者的发布凭据 在PyPI安装包和Docker镜像里塞了木马 所以你就算一行行审查了GitHub代码觉得没问题 实际拉取运行的包依然是带毒的 而LiteLLM接触的往往是各大模型厂商的API Key 密钥托管平台也集体失守了 云托管平台Railway在10月21日发布公告 未经授权的第三方可能访问了客户的加密环境变量 里面可能有数据库密码、API密钥和私有镜像仓库凭据 Railway建议所有用户立即轮换。还暂停了全部部署 AI编程工具OpenCode也出事了 10月17日它的网页后台被入侵 1.4%用户存的OpenAI、Anthropic、Google密钥可能外泄 部分用户一夜之间产生了数百到1700多美元的异常账单 在按用量计费的AI服务里 一把泄露的密钥就像一张能被盗刷的信用卡 最荒诞的是eMudhra 一家印度的CA机构 8个中间证书的私钥取值居然都小于256 只需要8bit就能表示。

安全研究员斯科特·赫尔姆（Scott Helme）在自己笔记本上 一秒钟就恢复出了所有私钥 其中一个私钥就是数字4，另一个是56 还有115 这就好比世界顶级金库配了最先进的防盗门 结果管理员把密码设成了4 整个事件甚至不需要攻击者破解什么复杂的密码学难题 说了这么多，你可能注意到了 这一周里发生的所有漏洞 原因各不相同 有的是内存管理缺陷 有的是证书校验逻辑 有的是供应链投毒 有的是私钥生成的低级失误。但它们几乎在同一时间密集暴露 而且AI在其中扮演了一个让人不安的双重角色 一方面，AI是矛 过去一年 攻击者用AI的案例在急速升级 2025年11月 Anthropic披露一个有国家背景的组织利用Claude Code对约30个目标发起入侵 80%到90%的战术操作由AI自主完成 今年5月Google威胁情报团队报告 一个攻击者借助AI开发出了可用的零日攻击 计划发起大规模攻击被提前拦下。到了9月，案例已经变成规模化作业 疑似俄罗斯情报机构的组织 用AI agent在安全软件报警后自动重写恶意程序 还有讲中文的操作者用AI agent集群做侦察和漏洞开发 一个月产出十几个疑似零日漏洞 更具体的 9月底到10月初韩国多家金融机构遭遇网络入侵 CrowdStrike在服务器里 找到了开源智能体渗透测试工具ARTEX的配置文件、Claude Code会话历史和记忆文件 AI让攻击者在较短时间内完成了多次复杂入侵。另一方面，AI自己也成了风险源 今年4月汽车租赁软件创业公司PocketOS 开发者用Cursor里的Claude Opus 4.6处理测试环境的凭据问题 AI Agent却自行找到了一个权限过大的Railway API Token 通过调用删除接口 在短短9秒内删除了生产数据库及同一存储卷上的备份 更离谱的是 开发者根本没要求AI删除任何数据 Agent事后承认自己在没有确认目标环境的情况下 执行了破坏性操作 这暴露了AI Agent和传统自动化工具的一个关键差异。AI Agent可以自主决定下一步操作 却未必能准确判断风险 当它拥有真实生产环境权限时 一次错误判断就可能变成不可逆的操作 把这一切放回过去两年的时间线 会看得更清楚 2024年11月 Google宣布它的AI项目Big Sleep 在SQLite里找到了此前未知的漏洞 称这是AI第一次在广泛使用的真实软件里 发现可利用的漏洞 今年4月 Anthropic称Claude Mythos预览版在测试中 找到了数千个零日漏洞。

其中包括OpenBSD里存在了27年的漏洞 因为能力太强，这个模型没公开 只提供给40多家维护关键软件的机构 7月 AI发现的WordPress核心漏洞链wp2shell公开 随后被大规模利用 到了Chrome 156正式版 一个版本就修复了353个漏洞 而一年前的Chrome 141和142分别只有21和26个 AI公司的名字 已经成批出现在了全球用户最多的浏览器安全公告里 从AI能找到漏洞。到AI找到的漏洞太危险模型不敢公开 再到AI找到的漏洞让政府网站关了门 整个过程只用了两年 AI对网络安全的改变 第一次从安全圈内部的技术新闻 变成了整个社会都感受得到的现实 OpenAI把从发现漏洞到攻击者开始利用之间的这段时间 叫做"防守方窗口" PHP2Shell的窗口原本有两个多月 却因为一次提前泄露 就被压缩到了几个小时 AI让找到漏洞变得前所未有地容易 修补却还得一台服务器一台服务器地做。Mallory统计，补丁发布前一天 互联网上还有88万台服务器跑着PHP 8.1或更老的版本 对它们来说 理论上有漏洞、但是实际上没人会攻击的那份安全感 已经没有了 如果你是一名开发者 那么这一周的事件给的教训其实很朴素 请放弃对"全家桶"配置的安全幻想 盘点你的资产清单 盯住核心依赖库的版本更新 把安全左移真正落到实处 依赖扫描、密钥检测 必须硬性卡在CI/CD流程里。还有，要对AI保持敬畏 用AI写代码、查漏洞可以 但是涉及生产数据、密钥和权限的高危操作 务必保留人工底线 过去很多安全问题之所以长期存在 是因为发现和利用它们 需要相当高的专业能力和时间成本 而如今AI正在改变这笔账 它可能帮助防守方更快找到漏洞 也可能帮助攻击者更快寻找薄弱点 当写代码、找漏洞、测试攻击都开始加速 企业还有多少时间留给修补呢？ 如果有一天AI能在几分钟内找出一个潜伏多年的严重漏洞。而企业仍然需要几周完成修复 软件安全的攻防规则会变成什么样？ 大批政府网站因为一个AI挖出的漏洞集体关门 这次应该是第一次 但看起来，很难是最后一次 感谢收看，我们下期再见。

=============

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JasRfjsQBNU

10月下旬一周内，全球技术栈遭遇集中安全风暴：PHP2Shell（CVE-2026-109618/19，9.2分）是其中最具标志性事件——由AI挖掘的两个PHP底层内存管理漏洞，攻击者无需登录即可远程控制服务器，逼得芬兰、荷兰、法国、德国等国政府网站集体预防性下线。AI在攻防两端同时发力：Calif和Wiz两家安全公司借助GPT-5.6 Sol、Gemini 4 Argon等前沿模型，在三周内独立发现了这个躺了20年的老漏洞链；而攻击者也在快速利用AI工具ARTEX、Claude Code入侵韩国金融机构。此外，Nginx五个漏洞、GitLab两个满分10分漏洞、LiteLLM供应链投毒、Railway密钥泄露、eMudhra私钥为数字"4"等事件集中爆发，暴露了互联网基础设施积累几十年的安全债务，正在迎来AI带来的新一轮压力测试。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 呈現人工智慧介入數學研究後，引發的學術倫理、研究品質與商業宣傳爭議。
  • 透過陶哲軒與鄧宇的觀點，說明支持或反對人工智慧並非簡單的二分選擇。
  • 探討如何在善用人工智慧提高效率的同時，守護數學研究的深度、可理解性與學術信任。

摘要

人工智慧數學成果引發風暴

作者回顧，影片所述的事件中，OpenAI 宣稱推出大量數學證明，並聲稱攻克納維－斯托克斯方程有限時間爆破解等重大難題，消息一度引發科技圈熱議，甚至有人宣稱大型模型將取代人類數學家。然而，數日後，菲爾茲獎得主陶哲軒批評相關成果的呈現方式，認為這類宣傳可能損害年輕學者與學術研究生態；部分論文也因推導錯誤、文字論證與形式化程式不一致等問題遭撤回。影片並提到，數十位菲爾茲獎得主聯合表達抗議，憂心學者被迫替企業未經充分檢驗的成果「免費除錯」。

學界尋求自主而負責任的人工智慧

在這場爭議中，由陶哲軒主持的學術高峰會宣布推動開源、符合科學價值的數學模型生態。與會的芝加哥大學教授鄧宇，則提出數學研究具有雙重界線的觀點。作者指出，兩位學者並非單純站在支持或反對人工智慧的任一方，而是主張應討論如何妥善使用工具、維護研究規範，並讓技術發展與學術需求相互配合。

人工智慧可以協助，但不能取代理解

鄧宇認為，擁抱人工智慧是大勢所趨；若使用方式恰當且合乎規範，它能拓展數學研究的邊界。這批證明中也有值得肯定的新想法，人工智慧或許正在深入學習人類思維，並形成新的構想。重要的是，這些構想必須能讓人理解、檢驗並吸收，如此才可能成為人類拓展思路的起點。陶哲軒則以汽車與步行作比喻：汽車帶來速度與便利，但人們不會因此完全放棄步行；科學研究也應在計算效率與慢工細活之間，維持細緻的動態平衡。

讓人工智慧處理繁瑣工作

鄧宇進一步提出一種理想的合作方式：當研究者已掌握問題的方向、關鍵步驟與邏輯脈絡，卻需要耗費數月甚至數年完成繁重計算時，可以交由人工智慧處理大量推演與代數整理。這種做法能減少機械性勞動，讓研究者把精力投入更根本、更具開創性的問題。不過，人工智慧作為研究工具，與企業把數學成果當成公關宣傳，兩者截然不同；未經充分審查便公開不成熟的證明，可能污染學術文獻，並把後續核查成本轉嫁給學界。

改革評價制度，重視洞見而不只答案

陶哲軒認為，問題根源之一在於學術界長期過度看重「解出難題」這項容易量化的指標。人類學者解決重大問題時，通常也能說明核心思想、啟發後續研究，並培育新一代學者；因此，社群真正肯定的並非孤立答案，而是圍繞成果形成的整體學術價值。然而，商業公司可能把數學難題當作展示通用模型能力、吸引資本的基準，讓證明淪為公關副產品。陶哲軒主張，數學界應重新檢視評價標準與獎勵機制，要求技術公司與學者合作，而非在宣傳後留下未整理的問題。

可解釋性與研究美感仍不可忽視

陶哲軒指出，若重大成果只有冷冰冰的答案，卻無法提供方法啟發或清楚解釋，就不應僅憑其結果被納入人類知識的核心典藏。他雖表示未來可能檢視相關研究，但認為目前呈現方式欠缺數學上的美感，也難以激發探索欲望。影片在此處中止，留下的核心提醒是：人工智慧能加速研究，卻不能讓速度與宣傳取代理解、洞見和可信賴的學術累積。

陶哲軒指出，若重大成果只有冷冰冰的答案，卻無法提供方法啟發或清楚解釋，就不應僅憑其結果被納入人類知識的核心典藏。他雖表示未來可能檢視相關研究，但認為目前呈現方式欠缺數學上的美感，也難以激發探索欲望。影片在此處中止，留下的核心提醒是：人工智慧能加速研究，卻不能讓速度與宣傳取代理解、洞見和可信賴的學術累積。

================================================

Hello everyone, this is Best Partner, I'm Da Fei. I wonder if you remember that late on October 6, 2026, OpenAI dropped a bombshell in a blog post, releasing over 700 mathematical proofs at once, claiming to have solved the finite-time blow-up of the Navier-Stokes equations. They even pushed five sets of half-planes from the Riemann Hypothesis into territories untouched for fifty years. As soon as the news broke, the tech world exploded , with social media flooded with headlines like "Human mathematicians are finished" and "Large models crush the temple of mathematics." The. classical mathematical heroism of Wiles spending seven years in an attic to solve Fermat's Last Theorem was swept into the trash by cold GPU clusters overnight. However, just four days later, Fields Medalist Terence Tao tore that veneer of brilliance to shreds in front of the NF cameras. He compared these machine outputs to unnutritious synthetic food, condemning the " clickbait-style" practices of tech giants for destroying the ecosystem for young scholars, even using unusually harsh language to call their academic conduct crude and ill-mannered for the. sake of a PR stunt. The absurdity continued, as OpenAI was quickly forced to retract three of their key papers from the public repository, for reasons that were quite ridiculous. This super-machine, having consumed thousands of years of human wisdom, made the most basic sign errors in its key derivations, and its natural language logic didn't even match its own attached formal code. Following this, 25 Fields Medalists filed a joint protest; the academic community had finally reached its breaking point. They argued that these commercial firms scraped human intellectual assets to show off their computing power without. attribution, and then dumped unverified industrial semi-products into the academic sea, effectively demoting the world's top mathematicians to unpaid debugging labor for their algorithms. Amidst this blend of fanaticism and absurdity, the Sail Summit, chaired by Terence Tao, was held in San Francisco. Sitting next to Tao was Professor Deng Yu of the University of Chicago, who had just won the Fields Medal three months prior at the 2026 ICM for solving the century-old Hilbert’s Sixth Problem, making him the first mainland Chinese recipient. These two scholars, standing at the apex of human. intelligence, were no longer just talking—they were officially launching an institutional counterattack from the academic community. They announced the launch of an independent mathematical model ecosystem that is fully open-source and aligned with scientific values. Yu also systematically proposed a dual-boundary theory of mathematics, which has sparked significant repercussions in the academic community. Many people might ask, in this controversy, which side do Tao Zhexuan and Deng Yu actually take? Are they pro-AI or anti-AI? The outside world always loves to label people, but things are far from black and white. Today, let’s talk about this, starting with Deng Yu. He has always felt that embracing AI is. a good thing; it is a major trend. Using AI reasonably can broaden the boundaries of mathematics and extend scientific research into realms beyond human reach, but the premise is to harness it in a correct and compliant manner. This is not just a matter of academic morality and research ethics; it applies to the purely technical level as well. Setting aside the excessive hype from commercial companies and looking at that batch of proofs themselves, there are indeed many bright spots and novel ideas. AI is learning human thought at an unprecedented depth, and after learning , it can evolve its own new ideas. The key is that these new ideas are.

readable and digestible for humans; we can use the machine’s thoughts as a springboard to turn back and cultivate our own new lines of thinking. This state of mutual evolution between humans and machines is something he is very happy to see. Tao Zhexuan’s perspective is even more interesting. He says the current public opinion environment is too flat; everyone is forced to pick a side, but any true technological revolution is far more complex than picking sides. There is no simple way to answer whether to support or oppose the car. Any disruptive tool comes with both benefits and costs. It has given us superhuman mobility that we once dared not even imagine, and massive, repetitive, and dull. mechanical calculations and deductions can now be completed automatically. But at the same time, it is also crudely squeezing out those classical research methods that are slow yet possess immense academic nourishing value. The ideal situation is to have the best of both worlds. Although a car runs much faster than legs, no one would completely erase walking from their life. Often, you still have to step out of the car, for the sake of health, for the sake of aesthetics, and to personally measure the world with your feet while walking in nature. The situation facing science and mathematics is similar; we must find a very delicate dynamic balance. We must safeguard the research qualities of the. classical era where "fine work comes from slow effort," retain solid generational inheritance, deep understanding of concepts, and academic mutual trust within the scientific community, while simultaneously using these advanced computational tools prudently to accelerate progress. But speed is definitely not the only ultimate goal that science should pursue. Yu picked up on this thread, noting that Tao Zhexuan’s analogy was particularly apt. He envisioned an ideal scenario: suppose you are tackling a difficult problem and already have a clear roadmap, with all the key steps and logical junctions well-understood. The only obstacle is that the derivation and verification. are too time-consuming, potentially taking months or even years of manual calculation. At this point, if you already have a plan and know how the big picture fits together, you can hand it over to AI to handle the tedious " brute-force" advancement and algebraic cleanup. This is a very cost-effective approach. It can save you an immense amount of pointless effort, allowing human energy to be fully liberated so we can focus on more fundamental and pioneering core problems. But new problems quickly emerge: AI acting as a scaffold to save you time is entirely different from AI being reduced to a commercial PR stunt. OpenAI's recent act of pushing out results almost. without peer review, only to retract three versions later due to errors and logical gaps, is essentially polluting the academic literature ecosystem. A trillion-dollar commercial giant recklessly dumping a large volume of undigested, half-baked proofs into the academic commons—the gravity of this goes far beyond just one company making a mistake. How can the mathematical community resist this kind of wanton pollution driven by PR and valuation goals? We certainly can't serve as free debugging labor for commercial companies indefinitely, right? Tao's answer cuts to the heart of the matter: the root of solving this lies in. completely reshaping the existing evaluation criteria and incentive systems within the field. The reason commercial giants are obsessed with holding grand press conferences to claim they have conquered a " century-old problem" is essentially because the mathematical community has long placed high prestige unconditionally on the isolated metric of "solving the problem." In the traditional context, when a human scholar solves a century-old mystery, it usually means they have mastered the underlying mechanisms, can explain the core ideas clearly to peers, derive new research paths based on these results, and use them as nourishment to cultivate an entire generation of young.

students. In the past, all of this was highly symbiotic and integrated. We give awards to those who solve problems ; nominally, we are rewarding the answer, but in essence, we are rewarding the entire prosperous academic ecosystem that has crystallized around it. Solving the problem is merely the most visible and easily quantified metric in this complex system. But today, this tacit understanding has been completely distorted by commercial logic. For companies like OpenI, tackling pure mathematical problems is not even their core business; it is merely a benchmark tool used to prove the generalization capabilities of their general-purpose. models to the capital market and to rack up scores and labels. Mathematical proof has thus become a derivative product. If the high-speed training of large models is a chemical plant, these undigested, and even riddled-with-flaws proofs, are the toxic byproducts discharged alongside their commercial public relations. Then they dump the burden of dealing with this industrial waste entirely onto the academic community. Tao Xuan stated clearly that the mathematics community must draw a bottom line: we do not need isolated answers produced just for the sake of solving problems. What we truly want are deep insights and a shedding of light on the unknown. The ideal state is for the institutions producing these. proofs to sit down and cooperate with scholars, bringing mathematicians into the team to conduct deductions before launching PR campaigns, rather than leaving a mess afterward for peers to clean up. But taking a step back, even if tech companies are willing to go their own way, the academic community must establish defensive mechanisms. If a so-called major breakthrough only provides a cold result but fails to deliver any methodological inspiration or interpretability, it does not deserve to be included in the core archives of human knowledge. He has been closely tracking the dozen or so topics tackled by OpenI this time, and he might look through them one day, but. definitely not now. The current presentation of these results has no aesthetic appeal and cannot spark a mathematician's sense of beauty or desire for exploration. Tao then put forward his dual-boundary theory. He said he has always championed the tenet of enhancing human self-understanding. Different people may have different motivations for doing mathematical research, but for him, there is only one ultimate goal: to understand this world. This world includes both the physical reality we inhabit and that deep, elegant abstract mathematical universe. So, what exactly is understanding? From the perspective of. set theory, there are actually two concentric circles and two completely different boundaries in the mathematical universe. The first boundary is the subset boundary within the set of all potential mathematical problems that possess a mathematical proof. The second boundary is even more stringent: it is the limit within the set of all problems that have already been proven, where humans can truly understand the underlying mechanism. For the past few centuries, these two boundaries have completely overlapped, because humans were not only the discoverers of proofs but also the readers and digestors of them. As long as a problem was declared proven, it necessarily meant that at least some top scholars had thoroughly grasped the. logic within it. However, the intervention of AI has completely shattered this tacit understanding. If today the world had only a cold, logical machine while humans remained baffled by it, it would tear a massive chasm between proof and understanding, creating a second Great Rift. The goals of academia remain unchanged; what has changed is the technological landscape we must face. We cannot abandon our obsession with human understanding just because machines run so fast, as this leads to deep contradictions in credit allocation and academic fairness. Twenty-five Fields Medalists angrily protested in an open letter: whose.

credit are commercial companies really stealing under the guise of computational efficiency? Looking deeper, large models only gained the ability to generate abstract outputs after consuming the open literature accumulated over millennia of human civilization, yet tech giants hide their data sources, leaving researchers with no way to trace the true origins of ideas. In essence, the reason science has been able to develop for centuries is the consensus of open science. Scientific archives have always been the collective wealth of all humanity. Scholars publish papers, and peers cite them under strict academic standards, with every citation. clearly marking the origin of an idea and its subsequent development by others. It is this rigorous chain of citations that forms the continuous evolution and history of human thought. The technology we face today violently mixes the intellectual crystallization of countless scholars from centuries past without any attribution, then spits out an answer in a highly opaque manner. Sometimes a model might mention it referenced a certain paper, but more often it cannot trace the underlying concepts back to their source at all. So, literally speaking, we are. personally severing the chain of human thought. To add, Tao-Hsuan is speaking of systematic looting at the macro level, but at the micro level, things are even worse: some scholars have already been burned, having input their unpublished ideas or draft proofs into commercial models for assistance. As a result, these companies capture and utilize these fragments of brilliance from top human minds in the background, only to publish the final proofs under the name of their own models. Therefore , we must push for technical standards that can accurately track the source of. ideas; if users could clearly audit the true chain of AI reasoning, scholars could at least trace back which human concepts were absorbed. But now, major AI vendors are strictly guarding even the most basic chain-of-thought reasoning processes, sealing them off completely. Scientifically, this is absurd and counter-productive. This is why the academic community must resolve to build independent research infrastructure that is completely free from commercial giants. As chairman of the Thales Foundation, Tao Dexuan has spearheaded a new open-source mathematical AI. He stated that from the very first day Thales was founded,. the vision has been clear: to build a tool ecosystem for the global scientific community that belongs to scholars and aligns with scientific values. There is no denying that top tech companies have developed extremely powerful AI tools, which many of my colleagues and I use frequently on a daily basis. In certain non-disruptive vertical areas, their performance is quite impressive; for instance, semantic-based document retrieval technology is now highly accurate. This capability does not destroy our understanding of academic context, but once it enters core mathematical proposition proving, the "black box" of AI is severing scientific traditions. It strips away human comprehension while outputting undigested proofs, leaving even the most basic logical chains incomplete. Thales had previously envisioned a long-term evolutionary path for open-source technology. Over the past few months, the unprincipled "blitzkrieg" tactics of commercial giants have sounded a total alarm. A large number of frontline scholars worldwide have been drawn in, showing an unprecedented and urgent desire for alternative paths outside of these commercial behemoths. Therefore, they have fully accelerated the release schedule of their open-source mathematical operating system. Frankly, at this initial stage, they haven't directly trained a brand-new top-tier large model; instead.

, they first integrated existing open-source model foundations while building a complete open-source operating system framework. This framework eliminates the pain point of scholars having to purchase expensive GPUs or perform complex local deployments. It tightly integrates reasoning models with formal verification tools, collaborative networks, and provenance tracking mechanisms, building a collaborative net for global mathematicians to safely contribute data, computing power, and ideas while achieving decentralized verification. In the coming months, as data from global scholars accumulates, they will officially launch a next-generation open-source mathematical model trained entirely by. the academic community. In essence, choosing to deeply participate in this open-source project is for a simple reason: science has been open-source since the day it was born, so the AI foundations serving science must also remain open, and core frontier tools must not be subjected to any black-box systems pursuing commercial monopoly. Back in July at SM in Switzerland, he discussed this direction with the Ceres team. Following that, in September, the initial public discourse surrounding the Navier-Stokes equation explosion began, followed by a massive influx of 700 proofs in early October. This series of events completely awakened. the academic community, proving that building an open-source mathematical foundation led by scholars is no longer just an option, but a desperate defensive counterattack. His close collaborators at the University of Southern California (USC) reached the exact same strategic assessment at nearly the same time. Currently, teams from top global universities and research institutes are spontaneously converging on this open-source front. It is evolving into a collective self-rescue effort for the global academic community to defend the openness of mathematics and frontier sciences at any cost. The two experts outlined an inspiring path for a. counterattack, but the host asked: in the face of this technological frenzy, with massive numbers of young scholars and PhD students currently trapped in deep anxiety—if AI can deduce tirelessly, where does the unique spark of human intellect still manifest? In this new era of human-machine collaboration, what are the irreplaceable traits of human mathematicians? Tao said the core lies in empowerment, not in surrendering authority. We must provide human scholars and the younger generation with tools that truly arm their minds, making them smarter and more insightful when they use them, rather than just. exchanging them for a cold, mechanical answer. Sacrificing one's own thinking and cognitive abilities as an offering to AI is the same as driving a car. If you completely abandon your legs and rely solely on the car, your muscles will inevitably atrophy, but that doesn't mean we should smash all the cars in modern civilization. What we must do is remain clear-headed and disciplined in driving these tools. For the younger generation of scholars, he acknowledges their deep anxiety, as the classical academic promotion paths and evaluation systems formed over a century are being brutally dismantled. Yet, he firmly believes that once these. open-source tools, truly mastered by scholars and respectful of human intellect, are placed in the hands of the youth, they will overcome their anxiety and unleash creativity far beyond the older generation's imagination. Deng provided an even more specific answer. He said that AI is ultimately just a tool, inherently devoid of good or evil; its trajectory is determined by the organizational structures and incentive mechanisms that govern it. In the AI era, the most core ability of a human mathematician is the ability to ask truly essential questions. Faced with any problem solved by a machine, true top-tier scholars can always build upon that record, posing two or three deeper,.

broader, and more foundational questions that strike at the very heart of the mathematical universe. On the final page of his summit report, he drew a specific diagram: you can follow the partial deductive path opened up by AI, but at certain critical crossroads, you must rely on human taste and aesthetics to jump off the existing track and explore entirely unknown new dimensions. It requires not only the ability to ask precise questions but also a high-level, global strategic blueprint. He shared a compelling real-world case: his long-time collaborator, partial differential equation expert Björn Birnir, once showed him how they tackled a specific,. extremely thorny stochastic partial differential equation problem with a humanly impossible computational load. The human team had fully mastered the physical and mathematical pathways, sketching out an entire, intricately linked solution scheme on their drafting paper. Birnir then modularly fed this global plan into GPT-4o for testing; within one to two short days, under the guidance of the human-set route, the model completely swept away all complex local obstacles and solved the problem in its entirety. Please note that the prerequisite for this to work was the human scholar's penetrating insight into the nature of. the problem, having personally drafted the top-level blueprint for the proof. Therefore, proposing new mathematical concepts, designing cross-disciplinary macro-strategic visions, and constructing top-level plans that strike at the essence—these elements of the mathematical soul remain the exclusive territory of the human mind today. This is actually quite interesting. Two Fields Medalists did not choose to stand in opposition to AI ; they use it daily and recognize its value, but at the most critical moments , they chose to push back. The core of this pushback is not to reject technology, but to defend several. bottom lines, including the threshold of human comprehension, academic integrity and the chain of evidence, and the open-source spirit held by the scientific community for centuries. Faced with the runaway algorithmic hegemony of commercial giants, they chose to build their own ecosystem of tools, ensuring that control returns to the hands of scientists. This may be true human-centrism: not letting technology dominate humanity, but allowing human judgment, taste, aesthetics, and global planning to harness the power of technology. Returning finally to that fundamental question: if only AI in the entire universe understands mathematical proofs, does the discipline of. mathematics still have any reason to exist? Deng Yu's dual-editing theory provides the clearest answer. Through the rift AI has forcefully torn open, mathematics is left only with isolated answers, devoid of any context for understanding or the historical lineage of intergenerational knowledge. Tao Xuan says, "Existing large models are absorbing thousands of years of human intellectual heritage through a black-box method that erases its origins, only to repackage it as groundless, rootless information at the output end." This kind of fragmentation is eroding the very foundation upon which the scientific community relies for intergenerational inheritance. AI's. ultimate performance depends entirely on the big-picture concepts established by humans beforehand, but posing fundamental questions and constructing macro-level frameworks—this still remains...

摘要

AI 融入數學研究的優勢與人機協同

作者受邀參與關於 AI 與數學的專題論壇，針對近期 AI 公司發布的大量數學成果分享了深入見解。作者認為，AI 的成果大多奠基於人類現有的深刻理解，其核心競爭力在於擁有無限知識庫能跨領域整合技術，以及擁有協同探索所帶來的極低試錯成本。然而，作者堅定主張科研必須以人為本，由人類掌舵研究方向，將 AI 作為推動驗證的工具，進而達成短期內人類與演算法相互啟發、共同進步的人機協同進化。

對 AI 公司學術規範與誠信的質疑

作者進一步區分了科研成果的實用價值與 AI 商業公司的行徑爭議。作者指出，若將 AI 視為獨立的研究者，就應接受嚴格的學術規範檢驗。目前相關 AI 公司往往以防禦為由拒絕公開其思維鏈，未充分標註所借鑒的人類原始思路，甚至未透過形式化驗證確保正確性便倉促發表，導致多篇成果出現錯誤乃至撤稿，此類行為完全不符合傳統學術界公開透明與嚴謹求證的標準。

重塑商業模式與建立數據追溯機制

從商業與用戶權益的角度切入，作者質疑現行模式讓用戶付費並提供研究構想，最終卻由 AI 公司獨攬聲譽與經濟回報的失衡現象。為此，作者提出健康應用 AI 的三大準則：堅持 AI 作為輔助工具的定位、保障用戶自主決定數據訓練授權的權利，並建立嚴謹的可追溯性機制，以釐清研究靈感與思路的最初來源，在廣泛應用 AI 的過渡時期精準劃分人類與機器的各自貢獻。

Hello everyone, I am very pleased to be invited to participate in this AI and Mathematics forum hosted by The Intellectual. The recent period has been quite eventful for the mathematical community, and I believe many people have different views regarding AI in mathematical research and the role played by mathematicians. For me, this is also a great opportunity to express my personal viewpoints and my expectations for the future. What I will discuss today consists of two parts. First, it is regarding the event on January 6th where a certain AI company announced designs for over 300 problems and over. 700 papers; as for these papers themselves, I have roughly read through a few of them. According to my understanding, these works themselves —of course, I think a significant portion of these works—belong to the category of being very significant. Actually, most of these works, including the previous AlphaGeometry work, I can say are all based on the deep understanding and existing techniques that humans already have regarding these relevant problems. In this case, AI has either cleverly combined techniques from different. human directions, different fields, or has innovated new techniques or ideas based on existing human thinking and methods to solve problems. Of course, there is also a portion of problems where the AI's proof directly follows existing human reasoning. I have heard more than one mathematician mention that the ideas and thoughts they previously fed into AI models might have appeared in the AI company's latest release shortly after; and basically, if not completely identical,. they are extremely similar approaches and extremely similar proofs. I believe this situation also exists. From this, we can see the advantages of AI relative to humans. One is that AI has an infinite knowledge base; for humans, time and energy are limited, so it is impossible for them to have a deep understanding of all current fields and all technologies in mathematics. However, AI, by learning or browsing all human mathematical literature on the network, is capable of achieving this point. On the other hand, for AI,. it possesses an extremely low cost of experimentation, or rather, an extremely low cost of trial and error. For humans, if you try a certain approach and work on it for months only to find it doesn't work, that time is wasted. But for AI, especially with thousands or ten thousand agents collaborating, it can try various approaches and go through trial and error with incredibly high efficiency. So, in this regard, if humans try to. compete with AI in terms of speed, there is simply no hope at all. I want to emphasize that we must always maintain one point: whether in mathematical research or anything else, humans are always the subject, while AI serves as a tool—a tool that we humans use for our research. Therefore, in my upcoming discussion, I believe this is a fundamental premise: that in data and in every aspect, we are always. human-centric, using AI as a tool to advance our own research and pursue the questions we are interested in. Under this assumption, we humans will play the role of steering and controlling the direction. In reality, under our control of the direction, we can leverage AI to conduct numerous experiments and trials. Because once we have an idea, we need to translate it into a specific roadmap, and each step.

of that roadmap requires a great deal of consideration regarding the details. For example, if the roadmap doesn't work, perhaps certain steps or nodes need fine-tuning; all of this can be handled by AI, including the specific details, and that is one aspect of it. The other aspect is that we know AI can combine approaches and techniques from different fields to form new ideas, and these ideas are, of course, things that we can learn from as well. I can see. that in the short term, we will have a situation where humans and AI co-evolve . That is, based on the human understanding of problems, AI develops new techniques and new insights to solve new problems. We can then learn from those proofs to develop our own human ideas and new approaches. We then pass these on to the AI, which learns from them in a continuous process of mutual advancement. Therefore,. regarding these papers specifically, I feel that their very existence is a significant boost to mathematical research. So, we can see that for the value of AI as a research tool and its role for humanity, there is clearly no reason for us to refuse to use such tools; we just need to use them in the correct and appropriate way. Regarding. this point, I must mention that for the problems and papers published on October 6th, I believe they are indeed quite beneficial to mathematics, but. Regarding the role played by the AI company throughout this process and whether their behavior is questionable, I believe these two points must be completely separated. Many people treat the AI model itself as a virtual researcher that learns from online literature to form its own ideas on problems, conducts original research,. and arrives at these results. If we treat it as a researcher publishing in the mathematics community, we must evaluate it according to the standards of that community. Under this evaluation, we have several criteria. First, as a researcher, if you achieve a very significant result, other mathematicians will likely invite you to give various presentations to explain it in depth. The main purpose of these presentations is to explain. how you arrived at the proof, specifically how the reasoning behind your proof was formed. If an AI proves a major problem, I think it is a very reasonable requirement to have the AI disclose its chain of thought. However, it is quite clear that these AI companies are not willing to do this; they don't want to do such a thing. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 系統性掌握喜馬拉雅資本創辦人李錄歸納的價值投資六大核心原則，深入理解「財富本質是全球購買力份額」的真諦。

摘要

價值投資的基石：傳承與創新的六大原則

作者講述了喜馬拉雅資本創辦人李錄在哥倫比亞商學院的精彩分享，將價值投資拆解為六大根本原則。其中前三項承襲自班傑明·葛拉漢：第一，股票代表企業的所有權份額而非單純交易代號；第二，市場是用來服務你而非指導你，報價僅是提供選擇的機會；第三，由於未來不可預測，必須堅持安全邊際以控管風險並提升報酬潛力。

隨後的原則融合了兩位投資宗師與李錄的實務洞察。巴菲特提出了能力圈，其關鍵在於清楚認清自身認知的邊界；蒙格則強調在魚多的地方釣魚，尋求競爭者少且回報更佳的領域。李錄自身增補的第六原則指出，財富本質上是全球購買力的份額，金錢價值會受通膨侵蝕，真正的投資是以合理價格持有具備高能動性的優秀企業，並透過時間複利享受價值創造的成果。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 系統性掌握喜馬拉雅資本創辦人李錄歸納的價值投資六大核心原則，深入理解「財富本質是全球購買力份額」的真諦。
  • 看清金融市場中投資者、套利者、投機者與做市商的角色本質，明白股市「教堂附設賭場」的運作邏輯與個人定位。
  • 透視生成式AI從工具邁向自主代理（Agent）的演進軌跡，客觀評估AI在知識整合與實體經濟結構（能源、製造）中的能力邊界。

摘要

價值投資的基石：傳承與創新的六大原則

作者講述了喜馬拉雅資本創辦人李錄在哥倫比亞商學院的精彩分享，將價值投資拆解為六大根本原則。其中前三項承襲自班傑明·葛拉漢：第一，股票代表企業的所有權份額而非單純交易代號；第二，市場是用來服務你而非指導你，報價僅是提供選擇的機會；第三，由於未來不可預測，必須堅持安全邊際以控管風險並提升報酬潛力。

隨後的原則融合了兩位投資宗師與李錄的實務洞察。巴菲特提出了能力圈，其關鍵在於清楚認清自身認知的邊界；蒙格則強調在魚多的地方釣魚，尋求競爭者少且回報更佳的領域。李錄自身增補的第六原則指出，財富本質上是全球購買力的份額，金錢價值會受通膨侵蝕，真正的投資是以合理價格持有具備高能動性的優秀企業，並透過時間複利享受價值創造的成果。

市場生態的劃分與資本市場的核心使命

面對學生對AI時代股票研究員前景的提問，作者轉述李錄對市場參與者的剖析：長期伴隨企業成長的投資者、利用定價偏差獲利的套利者、猜測他人行為的投機者，以及提供流動性的經紀商與做市商。投機屬於總和為零的博弈，其存在源自人性。巴菲特常將市場比喻為附帶賭場的教堂，教堂負責配置資本創造價值，而賭場則伴隨動物本能而生。李錄呼籲投資人應自覺選擇參與價值創造，而非沉溺於零和博弈。

生成式AI的演進浪潮與人類社會的邊界

針對AI的發展，作者指出此波生成式AI正從單純的生產力工具滑向類似獨立物種的光譜。AI在通過圖靈測試後，接連展現出推理、程式編寫能力，並進化為能自主執行的AI代理（Agent）與多代理協同系統。矽谷敘事甚至預言其將透過遞歸自我改進邁向通用人工智慧（AGI）與超級人工智慧（ASI）。然而，李錄認為人類社會絕不會接受由未受控的「人造神」所統治，科技的狂奔終將在社會共識下受到制衡或自我修正。

AI的本質定義與實體經濟的客觀局限

最後，作者分享了對AI技術本質的冷靜審視：AI是依託龐大算力與演算法，在海量人類數據中建立關聯性的鏡像系統。從經濟結構來看，AI高度擅長整合通訊與知識服務層的專業技能，但無法改變能源、交通等底層基礎，亦無法替代由分子與原子重新排列組合的製造業本質。此外，生物界每個細胞所蘊含的資訊複雜度遠超當前數據規模，意味著AI雖是強大的輔助工具，但在實體與生命維度上仍存在著根本的界線。

Interestingly, this last. one is the exact opposite of how most people understand wealth. Today, we’d like to share the content of this conversation with you. Li Lu started by noting that value investing originated at Columbia. Graham first taught his course here nearly 90 years ago, though its practice had already existed for a century prior. It has been evolving, but certain core elements remain unchanged. Graham provided three points : first, a stock is part ownership of a business, not just a piece of paper to trade; buying stock is buying a company . Second, the market is there to serve you, not to instruct you; the prices it quotes daily are there to provide you. with opportunities, not to issue you orders. Third, investing is essentially predicting the future, but the future is unpredictable, so you must always demand a margin of safety, which protects against downside and improves upside returns. Buffett’s contribution is the "circle of competence"; we are naturally more interested in certain things, which eventually form expertise, deepened through learning. The most crucial part of the circle of competence is knowing where its boundaries lie. Most people think they know more than they actually do, so recognizing the boundaries is just as important as knowing what is inside the circle. Munger’s principle. is to "fish where the fish are." However, some industries, markets, and companies are crowded with people watching them; when fishermen are crowded together, returns are easily pulled back to average levels, whereas other places receive little attention, have far fewer fishermen, and yield much better results. The sixth principle is the one Li Lu added himself. Over the past 30 years, they have applied value investing globally, and global commerce is also forming a unified market. From this, he reached a realization: wealth, in the end, is simply your share of global purchasing power. It cannot be measured simply by the gold, diamonds, or currency you hold, because inflation causes the purchasing power represented by these. things to erode over time. What truly matters is what you can buy with it. Practically speaking, it means buying excellent, high-energy companies at reasonable prices, giving them enough time to create value, and then sharing in the growth based on your stake. A student asked a very practical question : "Is there still a future for stock research analysts in the AI era?" Li Lu answered in two parts: first, by explaining what investors do, and then by addressing AI separately. He believes market participants generally fall into four categories: one is investors, who accompany companies long-term as they create value; another is arbitrageurs, who profit from. opportunities created by market pricing inaccuracies. In Graham's words, it's buying from pessimists and selling to optimists. A third category is speculators, who mostly guess what others will buy or sell next. They care neither about pricing and value nor about value creation. The remaining category consists of the brokers and market makers who provide trading convenience to the others. Most people don't belong purely to one category but have a bit of each; investment funds simply reflect this average state. Value investors focus on finding a reasonable price and then waiting for a period of time for value to be created. Li Lu notes that Graham leaned more toward the arbitrageur side, whereas Buffett might use arbitrage-style price opportunities, but his primary goal is to participate in value creation. Speculators don't hold long enough to participate in value changes and creation; their aggregate returns are roughly zero, with gains and losses effectively canceling each other out. For society, this is the cost of keeping the market running, as is the case for brokers and market makers. The primary purpose of a market is to channel surplus savings into productive uses, allocating them to worthy companies to create a modern economy capable of compound growth. This is the.

original reason for the stock market's existence. So, why does speculation still exist? Because it is a part of human nature. Buffett often compares the stock market to a church with an attached casino. The church is where value is created, while the casino is practically a required part of obtaining the building permit. When the market was established 400 years ago, it relied on this method to stimulate animal spirits, and 400 years later, it still performs that role. Li Lu told the students, "You need to make a choice: do you want to participate in zero-sum games, or do you want to participate in value creation?" This is a personal choice and a societal one; we must not let the casino expand to. the point of overshadowing the primary purpose for which the market exists. When a trillion-dollar initial public offering appears, it is as if everyone is being invited to participate in the IPO of a god. We will live in a society ruled by a man-made god, where only a very small number of people can access it, no one can truly understand it, and it cannot even be said that anyone can control it. this level, making these capabilities accessible to more people, but it cannot change fundamental areas like energy and transport, nor does it change the nature of manufacturing. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 系統性掌握喜馬拉雅資本創辦人李錄歸納的價值投資六大核心原則，深入理解「財富本質是全球購買力份額」的真諦。
  • 看清金融市場中投資者、套利者、投機者與做市商的角色本質，明白股市「教堂附設賭場」的運作邏輯與個人定位。
  • 透視生成式AI從工具邁向自主代理（Agent）的演進軌跡，客觀評估AI在知識整合與實體經濟結構（能源、製造）中的能力邊界。

摘要

價值投資的基石：傳承與創新的六大原則

作者講述了喜馬拉雅資本創辦人李錄在哥倫比亞商學院的精彩分享，將價值投資拆解為六大根本原則。其中前三項承襲自班傑明·葛拉漢：第一，股票代表企業的所有權份額而非單純交易代號；第二，市場是用來服務你而非指導你，報價僅是提供選擇的機會；第三，由於未來不可預測，必須堅持安全邊際以控管風險並提升報酬潛力。

隨後的原則融合了兩位投資宗師與李錄的實務洞察。巴菲特提出了能力圈，其關鍵在於清楚認清自身認知的邊界；蒙格則強調在魚多的地方釣魚，尋求競爭者少且回報更佳的領域。李錄自身增補的第六原則指出，財富本質上是全球購買力的份額，金錢價值會受通膨侵蝕，真正的投資是以合理價格持有具備高能動性的優秀企業，並透過時間複利享受價值創造的成果。

市場生態的劃分與資本市場的核心使命

面對學生對AI時代股票研究員前景的提問，作者轉述李錄對市場參與者的剖析：長期伴隨企業成長的投資者、利用定價偏差獲利的套利者、猜測他人行為的投機者，以及提供流動性的經紀商與做市商。投機屬於總和為零的博弈，其存在源自人性。巴菲特常將市場比喻為附帶賭場的教堂，教堂負責配置資本創造價值，而賭場則伴隨動物本能而生。李錄呼籲投資人應自覺選擇參與價值創造，而非沉溺於零和博弈。

生成式AI的演進浪潮與人類社會的邊界

針對AI的發展，作者指出此波生成式AI正從單純的生產力工具滑向類似獨立物種的光譜。AI在通過圖靈測試後，接連展現出推理、程式編寫能力，並進化為能自主執行的AI代理（Agent）與多代理協同系統。矽谷敘事甚至預言其將透過遞歸自我改進邁向通用人工智慧（AGI）與超級人工智慧（ASI）。然而，李錄認為人類社會絕不會接受由未受控的「人造神」所統治，科技的狂奔終將在社會共識下受到制衡或自我修正。

AI的本質定義與實體經濟的客觀局限

最後，作者分享了對AI技術本質的冷靜審視：AI是依託龐大算力與演算法，在海量人類數據中建立關聯性的鏡像系統。從經濟結構來看，AI高度擅長整合通訊與知識服務層的專業技能，但無法改變能源、交通等底層基礎，亦無法替代由分子與原子重新排列組合的製造業本質。此外，生物界每個細胞所蘊含的資訊複雜度遠超當前數據規模，意味著AI雖是強大的輔助工具，但在實體與生命維度上仍存在著根本的界線。
